name: The Nakumatt Envelope
description: During the ruracio negotiations for Miss Wanjiku Kamau, the groom's delegation presented an envelope intended to cover the first instalment of bride price. The envelope was opened by the bride's uncle and found to contain a Nakumatt loyalty card, a till receipt for Ksh 340, and a handwritten shopping list. The groom's spokesman requested a brief recess. The recess lasted three hours.
prose: The ruracio proceedings for Miss Wanjiku Kamau and Mr. Peter Njogu were convened on 22 November 2008 at the Kamau family homestead, Githunguri, Kiambu. The bride's family delegation comprised eleven persons, seated under the large fig tree at the rear of the compound. The groom's delegation, which had travelled from Limuru, comprised nine persons including Mr. Njogu's father, two paternal uncles, and the delegation's appointed spokesman, Mr. Zachary Mwangi, a teacher of some rhetorical reputation in the Limuru area.

Proceedings had advanced smoothly through the formal greetings, the presentation of sugar and tea, and the initial exchange of pleasantries. Mr. Mwangi had performed the spokesman's role with evident preparation, deploying two proverbs and a measured reference to the Njogu family's standing in their home area. The bride's family had received this well. At the point of presenting the first instalment envelope, Mr. Mwangi produced it from his jacket's inner pocket and placed it before the bride's lead uncle, Mr. Gideon Kamau, with appropriate ceremony.

Mr. Gideon Kamau opened the envelope. He looked into it for a moment longer than the situation required. He removed a Nakumatt loyalty card. He removed a till receipt, later confirmed to be from the Nakumatt Westlands branch, dated 21 November 2008, totalling Ksh 340 for two packets of unga, one bar of soap, and a tin of Kimbo. He removed a handwritten shopping list on a torn piece of paper. The list included milk, bread, and 'wire for fence — ask James.' There was no cash.

Mr. Mwangi requested a brief recess to consult with the delegation. The recess lasted three hours and fourteen minutes, during which the groom's delegation retired to their minibus in the compound. The bride's family was served tea twice. Mr. Njogu's father was observed making several phone calls. The correct envelope, containing Ksh 85,000 in cash, was produced upon the delegation's return. The ruracio was concluded successfully the same evening. Mr. and Mrs. Njogu have been married for sixteen years. The shopping list is held in private custody by Mr. Gideon Kamau, who has framed it.
heritageTrustNote: Mr. Gideon Kamau declined to surrender the framed shopping list to the archive but permitted a photographic record in 2023. Mr. Mwangi, when reached for testimony, stated only that it had been 'a long week.' He did not elaborate. The Heritage Trust has preserved this statement in full.

pullQuote.quote: Uncle Gideon held up the Nakumatt card and just looked at it. Nobody said anything. The birds were very loud that afternoon.
pullQuote.attribution: Miss Eunice Wangari, 34, Bride's cousin, Eyewitness
